lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Owned the monthly patient survey and the reporting dashboard the care teams used.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; my findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Wrote the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
- Improved dispute-form completion by 40% by splitting the form into three short steps with saved progress.
- Ran 18 moderated usability sessions a quarter from a recruiting panel of 400 customers, so every major release was tested with real account holders before launch.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Raised the onboarding flow's System Usability Scale score from 68 to 104 across two rounds of moderated testing with 20 customers.
- Validated the redesigned app navigation's findability with an open card sort of 30 customers before it shipped.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Published the design files and test protocol openly, and the city's transit agency invited the project to its spring accessibility review.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Conducted user interviews and created wireframes for a free clinic's online booking flow.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interviews, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed from a US-focused résumé.
items.because: They generally aren’t relevant to hiring.

items.says: Consider putting experience before education.
items.because: Recent work is now the stronger qualification.

items.says: Specify the survey and dashboard’s scope or a decision care teams made using them.
Clarify how the drop from 14% to 9% was measured.
Distinguish your research contribution from the team’s decision to build the reminder.
Say whether the change from two weeks to three days reflects a measured typical setup time.
items.because: The result is compelling if defensible.

items.says: Clarify the period or comparison behind the 30% reduction in support calls.
items.because: It would make the outcome credible.

items.says: Confirm that the 41% and 58% figures use comparable definitions and populations.
Avoid implying the design caused the entire increase in sign-ups.
items.because: A before-and-after result alone doesn’t establish that.

items.says: Make your research role in the dispute-form work clear.
items.because: It sounds as though you personally designed and implemented the form.

items.says: Specify whether 40% is a relative increase or a percentage-point change.
Clarify what you did with the usability findings.
items.because: The panel size and session count show scale but not what followed.

items.says: Make sure the claim that every major release was tested is supportable.
Fix the opening grammatical construction.
Separate the synthesis work from the 23% call reduction and explain the intervening change.
items.because: The line jumps from research methods to outcome.

items.says: A System Usability Scale score of 104 is impossible.
Check whether both testing rounds measured the same flow.
An open card sort alone cannot validate findability in the redesigned navigation.
items.because: It can inform grouping and labels, but does not establish findability.

items.says: Clarify which participants used screen readers versus low-vision accommodations.
Clarify whether the timed route-finding tasks were comparable.
The stated 50% improvement miscalculates the reduction in time.
items.because: Going from 90 to 60 seconds is a 33% reduction.

items.says: Distinguish changes for screen-reader users from those for low-vision users.
Check whether the spring accessibility review has happened and update the project status accordingly.
Add a distinct finding or decision from the interviews and wireframes, or remove this bullet.
items.because: It overlaps with the more specific testing bullet.

items.says: Explain how you determined the six issues were fixed.
Ensure the claim that two later volunteer teams used the handbook is verifiable.
Keep A/B testing only if you can discuss a real example.
items.because: None appears in the experience bullets.

items.says: Review whether methods used above, such as card sorting or accessibility research, are missing from the skills list.
Confirm that the job end date and the independent project’s “Present” status are current.
items.because: The job ends in June 2025 while the project says “Present.”
